title: Let a relay split one slice across several implementers
lead: The relay lets the owner split one slice's implementation into parts with disjoint files. Each part goes to its own implementer, for example several Haiku/xhigh implementers. One lead implementer owns the slice's tracking steps, and review and the gate see the combined diff once. A slice that is too big for one implementer should become two slices instead; a split is for one change that divides cleanly.
findings_note: owner request, session 2026-10-13: more than one Haiku/xhigh implementer per slice when it makes sense
boundary: **Not in this slice:** new tracking state for parts (no part records, sub-items or per-part claims; `start` stays one claim per slice), a worktree per part, slicer spawning or scheduling implementers, automatic partitioning, and choosing the agent per role (s257).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The owner asked to run more than one implementer on a slice when that makes sense, especially Haiku at xhigh (session 2026-10-13). Smaller, file-scoped briefs suit a small model better than one long brief. Parallel parts also cut wall time on a slice whose code, tests and docs touch independent modules. The relay text now assumes one implementer that "owns one slice" and runs `start` and the close. With no rule for splitting, two implementers would both run tracking commands or edit the same files.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: src/slicer/ai.py (RELAY_HEAD Roles and Setup, RELAY_ORDER Order and Every brief, ROLES_SKELETON), tests/test_ai.py, docs/agents.md, CHANGELOG.md.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- New `test_RelayText_Setup_AsksWhetherToSplit`: Setup asks whether the implementation splits into parts, and says a split needs parts with disjoint files and their own tests.
- New `test_RelayText_Roles_LeadImplementerOwnsTracking`: Roles says that in a split, one lead implementer runs `start`, the note and the finish step, and part implementers change only their own files and run no slicer command that writes.
- New `test_RelayText_Order_SplitPartsThenOneReview`: Order says that parts with disjoint files may run in parallel in the slice worktree, otherwise one after another. The orchestrator runs the full suite on the combined diff, and one review and one gate cover the whole slice.
- New `test_RelayText_EveryBrief_PartBriefNamesItsFiles`: a part brief names its own files, the files it must not touch, and its own temp directory.
- `test_RelayInitRoles_NoFile_WritesSkeletonWithMatrixAndRules`: the skeleton has an example split row and the rule "Split a slice only into parts with disjoint files and their own tests; a slice too big for one implementer is two slices."
- `test_Relay_NamesNoVendorModelOrOutsidePath` stays green.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Setup: add a bullet asking whether the implementation splits into parts, with the disjoint-files-and-tests condition. The default is one implementer.
2. Roles: add the lead and part implementer sentences. The reviewer rule extends to every part: a reviewer wrote no part.
3. Order: add the split sequence, with parallel parts only when their files are disjoint, then the orchestrator's combined-suite run, then the single review and gate. Accepted findings go back to the part that owns the file.
4. Every brief: add the part brief contents.
5. ROLES_SKELETON: add an example row `| Implementer, per part | well specified, split into parts with disjoint files | Claude Code | Claude | haiku | xhigh |` and the split rule.
6. Update docs/agents.md and add a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry under Changed.
7. Mutation-check each new assertion.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- The full suite passes on Python 3.11+.
- `slicer ai relay` shows the split bullet in Setup and the split sequence in Order, and the generic text still names no product.
- `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s258`, branch `feature/s258-relay-split`. Commit only on the branch. Merging and pushing wait for the owner.
